subject: english
question: In the sentence, “The persistence of such barriers underscores the necessity for institutional reforms aimed at amplifying female representation in executive roles,” the phrase “aimed at amplifying female representation” is:

options.text: an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2) a participial phrase modifying “reforms”***

 
 
• This is the **correct** answer. The phrase begins with the past participle "aimed." It functions as an adjectival phrase directly describing the noun preceding it, "reforms." It tells us specifically what kind of institutional reforms are necessary—those that are aimed at amplifying female representation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (a misplaced modifier)**: Incorrect because it is placed perfectly adjacent to the noun it describes ("reforms"), meaning there is no grammatical ambiguity about what is being modified.
 
• **Option 3 (an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence)**: Incorrect because an absolute phrase typically features a noun or pronoun alongside a participle modifying the whole clause (e.g., "The reforms having passed, the board celebrated"), which doesn't fit the syntax here.
 
• **Option 4 (an infinitive phrase modifying “necessity”)**: Incorrect because an infinitive phrase requires the word "to" followed by the base form of a verb (e.g., "to aim").
